tasks.my_tasks.description: My Tasks (MyTasksPage, #249) — the work somebody has been given. Mounted in all three workspaces, which since 14 Oct 2026 is TWO routes off one component: the whole list and the `is_overdue` cut. `page` sits beside the h1 of the first, `is_overdue` beside the h1 of the second (one ⓘ each, never both); `status` on the list's status column. The deadline, priority and kind-of-work columns explain themselves.

page.hint: Work your manager or HR has given you. Opening a task tells them you’ve seen it, so they know it’s been picked up.

askMaya.question: How do assigned tasks work, and what happens after I hand one in for review?

status.hint: Not started and being worked on are yours to set. Waiting for review means it’s with your reviewer until they reply.

askMaya.question: What do the different task states mean, and which ones can I change myself?

is_overdue.hint: Past its deadline and not yet handed in. Handing one in takes it off this list, even if it is late.

askMaya.question: When does a task count as overdue, and does handing it in late still clear it?

tasks.task_detail.description: The task record inspector (TaskDetailDialog, #250/#258/#267), shared by all three planes. Core entries cover the state, the rework count, the read receipt and the original deadline. The onboarding tier adds the derived and governance figures HR reads: extensions, on-time completion, handovers, the audit trail and the email outbox.

status.hint: Where the task has got to. Only a reviewer can move it past Waiting for review — by approving it or sending it back.

askMaya.question: What are the stages of a task, and who can move it from one to the next?

rework_count.hint: How many times this has been sent back for changes. Each round keeps the same deadline unless somebody moves it.

askMaya.question: What happens when a task is sent back for changes, and does its deadline change?

first_viewed_at.hint: When the person it’s for first opened the brief. Until then they may not know about it, whatever the deadline says.

askMaya.question: How does the system know whether somebody has opened a task that was given to them?

original_due_date.hint: The deadline this task started with. It’s kept even after the deadline moves, so you can see the work was given longer.

askMaya.question: Why is the first deadline of a task kept after the deadline has been moved?

due_date.hint: The deadline in force now. Past it, the task shows as past deadline until it’s approved or called off.

askMaya.question: When does a task start showing as past its deadline, and does anything happen automatically?

extension_count.hint: How many times the deadline has been moved. Useful when deciding whether a task is genuinely blocked or just drifting.

askMaya.question: What does it tell me about a task if its deadline has been moved several times?

is_completed_on_time.hint: Worked out when the task was approved: whether that approval happened on or before the deadline in force at the time.

askMaya.question: How is a task judged to have been finished on time — by when it was handed in or when it was approved?

reassignment_count.hint: How many times this has changed hands. Each new person starts from an unopened task, and what was handed in stays on record.

askMaya.question: What happens to a task’s history and progress when it is handed to somebody else?

audit_logs.hint: Every change to this task, newest first — who did it and when. It can’t be edited, so it’s what to read when there’s a dispute.

askMaya.question: What is recorded in a task’s history, and can any of it be changed or removed later?

notifications.hint: Emails queued about this task. Queued means it is waiting for the sender to run, not that it has failed.

askMaya.question: Who gets emailed about a task, and what does it mean when a notice is still queued?

tasks.discussion.description: The conversation on one task (TaskDiscussion, #253/#254/#264). A section of the task record inspector, so it is seen in all three workspaces — by the assignee on their own task and by a reviewer on somebody else's. Written neutrally for both. The message box, the file picker and the timestamps explain themselves; what needed saying is the milestone flag we invented, the link rule the server enforces, and that nothing here can be taken back.

comments.hint: Everything said about this task, oldest first. Nothing here can be edited or deleted — to correct something, say so in a new message.

askMaya.question: Who can read the discussion on a task, and can a comment be edited or removed afterwards?

is_progress_update.hint: Marks this as a step finished rather than a chat message, so the thread can be filtered down to real progress. It does not move the task along.

askMaya.question: When should a task comment be marked as a milestone, and what changes when it is?

external_links.hint: Each link has to start with https:// and point to a public page. An address inside a private network is refused, to keep company systems out of reach.

askMaya.question: Why is a link sometimes refused when it is added to a task comment?

tasks.assign.description: Give out a task (AssignTaskDialog, #255 for a manager / #265 for HR). The title, the person and the description explain themselves. The deadline carries the 15-minute rule, and category and priority both need saying because neither changes how the task behaves. The onboarding tier covers the staged file upload.

due_date.hint: When the work is needed. It has to be at least 15 minutes away, and the time of day counts — past it the task reads as late.

askMaya.question: Why does a task deadline need a time of day as well as a date?

category.hint: Groups the task for filtering and reporting. It changes nothing about how the task behaves for the person doing it.

askMaya.question: What are task categories used for, and does the category change anything for the person assigned?

priority.hint: Tells the person what to do first. It doesn’t change the deadline or send anything extra — it’s guidance, not a rule.

askMaya.question: Does setting a task to urgent change anything beyond how it looks to the person assigned?

external_links.hint: Pages the work needs — a sheet, a document, a report. They see these in the brief, and a link must start with https://

askMaya.question: Why do task reference links have to start with https, and who can open them?

attachment_tokens.hint: Files sent with the brief. They upload as you pick them, so leaving this form open a long time can mean choosing them again.

askMaya.question: How are files attached to a task, and what file types and sizes are allowed?

tasks.submit.description: Hand in your work (SubmitTaskDialog, #252). Mounted wherever My Tasks is, so all three workspaces. Written to the person about their own work.

submission_note.hint: What your reviewer reads first. Say what you finished and anything they should check, not just that it’s done.

askMaya.question: What should I write when I hand in a task, and who reads it?

external_links.hint: Links to the work itself. These are added to the task’s links; nothing you add here removes what your reviewer put there.

askMaya.question: What happens to the links already on a task when I add my own while handing it in?

attachment_ids.hint: Files you’re handing in. They’re saved to the task as you pick them, so they stay even if you close this and come back.

askMaya.question: What file types can I hand in with a task, and how large can each one be?

tasks.review.description: The reviewer's reason prompts (TaskReviewDialogs, #259-#263). Each dialog already says in its own description who feels the consequence; the one field that needs a rule stated is the replacement deadline, shared by the hand-over and extend dialogs.

new_due_date.hint: The deadline they get instead. It has to be later than the one in force, and the original deadline stays on the record.

askMaya.question: When a task deadline is moved, what is the employee told and what is kept on the record?

tasks.assigned_tasks.description: Tasks I Assigned (TaskReviewScreen, scope assigned, #256), in the manager and HR workspaces alike. `page` beside the h1; `is_viewed` on the Opened column, which only this list has; `status` on the status column, written to whoever is reviewing.

page.hint: Work you’ve handed out. Approving, sending back and moving a deadline all happen here, from the task itself.

askMaya.question: What can I do to a task I have given somebody, and at what stage can I do each thing?

is_viewed.hint: When the person first opened the brief. Blank means they haven’t looked yet, which is worth chasing before the deadline.

askMaya.question: How can I tell whether somebody has actually opened a task I gave them?

status.hint: Waiting for review is the one that needs you: the work is in and the task sits still until you approve it or send it back.

askMaya.question: Which task states are waiting on me as the reviewer, and which are waiting on the employee?

tasks.employee_tasks.description: The Tasks tab on one person’s record (EmployeeTasksTab), in the HR and manager workspaces: #266 filtered by `assignee_id` for HR, #257 by `subordinate_id` for a manager. Same screen in both; the counts and the status column mean the same thing as on All Tasks.

page.hint: Everything this person has been given, whoever gave it out — not only the tasks you handed to them yourself.

askMaya.question: Whose tasks appear on an employee’s record?

status.hint: Waiting for review is the one that needs you: the work is in and the task sits still until you approve it or send it back.

askMaya.question: Which task states are waiting on a reviewer, and which are waiting on the employee?

tasks.all_tasks.description: All Tasks (TaskReviewScreen, scope all): #257 for a manager, their reporting line, and #266 for HR, the whole organisation. Same screen and labels in both; `department_id` is gated to HR because only #266 has that filter.

page.hint: Every task within your reach, whoever gave it out — so nothing sits unopened or past its deadline without being noticed.

askMaya.question: Whose tasks appear on this screen, and how is that different from the tasks I gave out myself?

status.hint: Waiting for review is the one that needs you: the work is in and the task sits still until you approve it or send it back.

askMaya.question: Which task states are waiting on a reviewer, and which are waiting on the employee?

department_id.hint: Narrows the list to people in one department. Somebody with no department on file won’t appear under any of them.

askMaya.question: Why might an employee be missing when I filter tasks by department?

attendance.my_devices.description: My Devices (MyDevicesPage), mounted in all three workspaces under each one’s own self-service prefix. REBUILT AS TWO SCREENS 22 Oct 2026 (user decision): the on-page tab strip is gone and the sidebar’s two entries are the navigation, so there is no single `page` key any more — each screen keys its own <h1> help. This device: this_device (h1), effective_mode (the mode pill beside it), device_bound (spec list) — 3. All my devices: all_devices (h1), effective_mode, status (column) — 3. Inspector: device_bound, last_ip, last_used_at (3); last_used_at lives here rather than on the table header, because spotting a device you don’t recognise is done with the record open. Written to the person about their own device, so these entries are never reused on an HR screen about somebody else.

this_device.hint: The device you’re on now, as long as you registered it in this browser. Registered it somewhere else? It’s under All my devices.

askMaya.question: Why can’t the page always tell which of my devices I’m using right now?

all_devices.hint: Every device you have registered, including ones you’ve shut off. Shut-off devices stay as a record and can’t be used to clock in.

askMaya.question: Why do devices I’ve shut off stay on my list instead of disappearing?

effective_mode.hint: What your organisation asks for today. On Required, a punch from an unregistered device is refused; on Watch only it still goes through.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between a device check that is only watched and one that is required?

status.hint: Ready means you can clock in from it. Waiting means HR hasn’t approved it yet. Blocked can be switched back on; shut off can’t.

askMaya.question: What do the states on my devices mean, and which of them let me clock in?

last_used_at.hint: When a punch was last accepted from this device. It is how you spot one you no longer use, or one you don’t recognise.

askMaya.question: How can I tell whether a device on my list is still one I use?

device_bound.hint: Yes means its screen lock stays on this device alone. No means your other devices share it, which your organisation may not accept.

askMaya.question: Why does it matter whether a device’s screen lock is tied to that one device?

last_ip.hint: Roughly where on the network the last punch came from. A hint for spotting something odd, not proof of who used the device.

askMaya.question: What does the network address on my device record tell me, and what does it not tell me?

attendance.device_registration.description: Register this device (RegisterDeviceDialog), raised from My Devices in all three workspaces. Only the replacement picker qualifies — the device name, and the code sent to confirm it, are ordinary fields and get nothing.

replace_device_id.hint: You already have as many devices as your organisation allows, so registering this one shuts off the device you pick. That can’t be undone.

askMaya.question: What happens to my old device when a new one replaces it, and can I get it back?

attendance.device_checks.description: HR — Setup › Organisation › Registered Devices (RegisteredDevicesPage). REBUILT 22 Oct 2026 (user decision): readiness was three cards above the tab bar, then one strip inside the People tab, and is now its own STATUS tab drawn as a RING — coverage_percentage on the heading and in the middle of the ring, and one legend row per slice keyed enrolled_users / pending_users / uncovered_users, each row the way to the people it counted. The three slices are mutually exclusive and sum to active_members: pending is carved OUT of the uncovered remainder, because a device waiting on approval cannot be used yet — so uncovered_users labels "Nothing registered yet", not everybody who is short. Page help is keyed page beside the <h1>; tab help is one ⓘ beside the tab strip keyed tab.<open tab> (people, settings, activity, status). People tab keys devices, last_used_at and coverage_state — the Can clock in column carries it alone, since the state filter became a <select> whose options spell themselves out (once per concept). Settings tab covers the policy payload keys, Activity covers events. Onboarding tier: every field here decides whether somebody else can clock in, so all of them are explained and the 4-per-screen cap does not apply.

tab.people.hint: Everyone in the organisation and what they have registered. Open somebody to see their devices, approve one, or shut one off.

askMaya.question: How do I find out who still needs to register a device?

tab.settings.hint: The rules behind the checks: what a device is needed for, how many each person may keep, and what happens before a new one works.

askMaya.question: Which device settings should I decide first when I’m setting this up?

tab.activity.hint: Every device decision and every refused punch, newest first. Where to look when somebody says they couldn’t clock in.

askMaya.question: How do I find out why somebody’s punch was refused?

tab.status.hint: How close the organisation is to everybody being able to clock in from a registered device, and whether it is safe to make one compulsory yet.

askMaya.question: What happens to people without a registered device once I make one compulsory?

devices.hint: What this person has registered, and how many of those can be used right now — a dot each for ready, waiting, blocked and shut off.

askMaya.question: What should I do when somebody has a device waiting and no working one?

coverage_state.hint: Whether this person can clock in today. “Waiting for you” needs your decision; “Needs a new one” means their only device was shut off for good.

askMaya.question: What stops an employee clocking in once device checks are compulsory?

last_used_at.hint: When a punch was last accepted from one of this person’s devices. Empty until they clock in from one.

askMaya.question: What does the last-used time tell me about an employee’s device?

page.hint: See who has registered a device for clocking in, and decide whether a punch has to come from one. Switched off, attendance works as it does today.

askMaya.question: What are device checks for, and how do I roll them out without stopping people clocking in?

enrolled_users.hint: How many people have at least one device ready to use. Only these can clock in once a registered device is compulsory.

askMaya.question: Who counts as having registered a device, and how do I get the rest of my people registered?

active_members.hint: Everyone still working here who could be asked to clock in. People who have left aren’t counted.

askMaya.question: Who is counted as working here for the purposes of device checks?

coverage_percentage.hint: How many of your people can already clock in from a registered device. Reach the mark on the bar before you make it compulsory.

askMaya.question: How high should device coverage be before I make a registered device compulsory?

uncovered_users.hint: People who haven’t registered anything that works yet. Make a registered device compulsory and these are exactly the people who could not clock in.

askMaya.question: What should I do about people who still have no registered device?

pending_users.hint: People waiting on a decision from you. Their device is registered but can’t be used to clock in until you approve it.

askMaya.question: What am I checking when I approve or reject somebody’s device?

enforcement_mode.hint: Off asks nobody. Watch only records which punches came from a registered device. Required refuses the ones that didn’t.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between watching device checks and requiring them, and which should I start with?

enforced_operations.hint: Which punches have to come from a registered device. Anything you leave out is accepted from any device, as it is today.

askMaya.question: Should I check every punch, or only clocking in and out?

enforce_from.hint: Nothing changes for anybody until this date, so people have time to register. Leave it empty and it applies as soon as you save.

askMaya.question: How much notice should I give people before a registered device becomes compulsory?

max_active_devices.hint: How many devices one person may keep at once. At the limit, registering a new one shuts off an old one they choose.

askMaya.question: How many devices should one employee be allowed to clock in from?

registration_approval.hint: Either the employee confirms with a code and the device works at once, or it waits in your queue until you approve it.

askMaya.question: Should I approve each new device myself, or let employees confirm their own with a code?

require_device_bound.hint: Refuses a screen lock the employee’s other devices share, because it can’t prove which device the punch came from.

askMaya.question: What is a synced screen lock, and why can it not prove which device someone punched from?

allow_platform_web.hint: Lets people register the browser on a laptop or desktop. Turn both this and the phone app off and nobody can register anything.

askMaya.question: Should I let people clock in from a laptop browser, a phone, or both?

allow_mobile_key.hint: Lets people register through the mobile app. Turn both this and the browser off and nobody can register anything.

askMaya.question: When would I allow only the phone app to be registered?

challenge_ttl_seconds.hint: How long somebody has to finish the fingerprint or screen-lock prompt before the check expires and they have to punch again.

askMaya.question: What happens if an employee takes too long at the fingerprint prompt when clocking in?

events.hint: What the checks have done: devices registered, punches refused, and the ones that would have been refused while you are only watching.

askMaya.question: How do I use the device activity log to tell whether it is safe to make device checks compulsory?

attendance.employee_devices.description: HR — Time & Leave › Employee Devices (EmployeeDevicesPage): the whole-organisation device inventory and the pending approval queue, also embedded in the HR Inbox. Onboarding tier; written about somebody else’s device, never reusing the employee’s own my_devices wording.

last_ip.hint: The browser, and roughly where on the network this device last punched from. Useful for spotting something odd, never proof of who used it.

askMaya.question: What can the network address on a device record tell me about where someone clocked in from?

page.hint: Every device your people may clock in from. Approve the ones waiting, and shut off devices somebody has lost or no longer uses.

askMaya.question: What should I check before I approve an employee’s device?

status.hint: Waiting needs your approval before the employee can clock in from it. Blocked can be switched back on later; shut off is permanent.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between blocking an employee’s device and shutting it off?

device_bound.hint: Yes means the screen lock stays on that one device. No means the employee’s other devices share it, so it can’t prove which one punched.

askMaya.question: Why does it matter whether an employee’s device has a screen lock shared with their other devices?

attendance.locate_employee.description: Asking one person's phone where it is, and the history of who asked before (LiveLocationPanel + LocateDialog on the employee profile's Reporting & Location tab, 2026-10-23). Shared by HR and the manager through the viewer prop, so the voice is neutral - 'the person', never 'your report'. The reason box is the only typed field; the rest of the dialog is read-back.

column.hint: Asks the person’s phone where it is right now. They are told who asked and why, and the answer is one position at that moment — not a trail.

askMaya.question: What happens when I ask a colleague where they are?

panel.hint: Ask this person’s phone where it is right now. They see a notice with your reason, and the request is recorded against your name.

askMaya.question: When is it fair to ask someone for their live location?

reason.hint: The person being located reads this, and it stays on the record. Say what you need to confirm rather than just “checking”.

askMaya.question: What makes a good reason for asking where someone is?

accuracy_meters.hint: How wide an area the position could really be in. A large number means the phone was indoors or on a weak signal, not that the person moved.

askMaya.question: Why is a phone’s location sometimes only accurate to a few hundred metres?

attendance.location_policy.description: The organisation-wide Live Location Checks policy (HR > Setup > Organisation, 2026-10-23). Every setting here lands on somebody else, so the whole screen is onboarding tier: an HR admin setting this up in their first month decides how closely colleagues can be checked. Keys are the PUT payload keys.

page.hint: Decide whether anyone here may ask a colleague’s phone where it is, who may ask, and how often. It starts switched off.

askMaya.question: What should I think about before turning on location checks?

enabled.hint: Off means nobody can ask anybody, whatever else is set here. Turning it on applies immediately to everyone you allow below.

askMaya.question: What changes for employees the moment location checks are switched on?

allowed_requester_roles.hint: HR admins can ask anyone; managers only their own direct reports. Pick at least one, or nobody can ask at all.

askMaya.question: Should managers be able to ask where their team is, or only HR?

consent_mode.hint: Whether people must read and accept the notice before anyone can be given their location, or are simply told each time it happens.

askMaya.question: What is the difference between telling someone and asking them to accept first?

notify_employee.hint: Whether the person’s phone announces each request. Turning it off means they are located without being told at the time.

askMaya.question: What are the risks of locating people without telling them?

require_reason.hint: Whether whoever asks must type why. The person being located reads that reason either way — this decides if it can be left blank.

askMaya.question: Why should a reason be compulsory for a location request?

require_clocked_in.hint: Whether people can only be asked during their shift. With this off, somebody can be asked on a day off or late at night.

askMaya.question: Why is it safer to allow location requests only while someone is clocked in?

request_ttl_seconds.hint: How long we wait for the phone to answer before giving up. Too short and a phone on a weak signal never gets the chance.

askMaya.question: What happens to a location request that nobody’s phone answers?

cooldown_seconds.hint: How long the same person must wait before asking the same colleague again. This is what stops somebody being checked over and over.

askMaya.question: How do cooldowns protect people from being checked too often?

max_requests_per_employee_per_day.hint: The most times one colleague can be asked in a day, counting everybody who asks. After that, further requests are refused.

askMaya.question: What happens once someone has been asked the maximum number of times today?

log_retention_days.hint: How long the positions themselves are kept before being deleted. Who asked, when and why is kept either way.

askMaya.question: How long should we keep the locations people’s phones send back?

attendance.my_location_checks.description: My Location Checks (shared self-service page, mounted in all three workspaces, 2026-10-23). Written to the person being located about their own data. The anti-spoof verdict and the position itself are withheld from this endpoint on purpose, so nothing here may hint at them.

page.hint: Everyone who has asked where you are, and the reason each of them gave. Nobody can ask without it appearing here.

askMaya.question: Who is allowed to ask for my location, and when?

consent.hint: Accepting records that you have read how this works. Until you do, your organisation may refuse every request for your location.

askMaya.question: What am I agreeing to when I accept the location notice?

fix_returned.hint: Whether your phone sent a position back. It won’t have if the phone was off, had no signal, or you weren’t clocked in at the time.

askMaya.question: What happens if my phone doesn’t answer a location request?
